docs.text: Fast. Usable. Affordable. RPN.

docs.title: The Philosophy
docs.text:
When I was in high school, I was the captain of the calculator team. My instrument of choice was a legendary tactile Reverse Polish Notation scientific calculator. It was fast, mechanical, and mathematically pure. For years afterward, throughout engineering school and research, I relied on postfix evaluation, always missing the physical immediacy of that tactile machine.

When my daughter started middle school and was finally allowed to use a calculator in class, I looked for an everyday, accessible RPN handheld for her. There were none. The market offered only two extremes: fragile, expensive vintage collectibles suited for display cases, or disposable in-fix graphing bricks covered in confusing parentheses syntax and battery compartments that corrode.

So I built my own.

StackCalc is not a retro novelty or a piece designed to sit behind glass for collectors. It is designed to be a fast, everyday mathematical instrument that you reach for when you need to solve real-world problems. Our mission is simple: end the cognitive friction of in-fix entry, unbind learners from the confusion of nested parentheses, and eliminate the forced equals sign once and for all.

  • Native Watch & Phone Digital Twin: Immediate access on modern everyday devices. It provides a tactile gateway to learn RPN before graduating to the dedicated hardware instrument.
  • Interactive Tutorials: Built-in guided learning modules demonstrating how the four-level stack evaluates expressions sequentially without syntax errors.
  • Deliberate Minimalism & Focus: We removed features common to distracting classroom devices for intentional pedagogical reasons:
  • No Complex Scripting: Kept intentionally non-programmable so it is fully compliant with ACT, SAT, and AP exam testing regulations.
  • No Radios or Touchscreen Distractions: Hardware firmware contains zero Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or camera hardware, ensuring 100% exam compliance and unbreakable classroom focus.
  • No CAS Black Boxes: Solvers are strictly numeric and evaluate via visible stack steps.
  • No Unwieldy Matrix Menus: Deep matrix algebra belongs on modern computational notebooks; everyday calculation belongs on an immediate, tactile handheld.

Geek out over the details with us. Welcome to StackCalc32.

docs.title: Detailed Regulatory Explanations
docs.text:
1. Absence of Wireless Communication Radios: The SC-32 mainboard uses a bare-metal Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller with zero radio peripherals. There are no antenna traces, Bluetooth modules, Wi-Fi chips, or infrared data links on the PCB. It is physically incapable of transmitting or receiving wireless signals.

  2. Strict Numerical Engine (No Symbolic CAS): Prohibited CAS calculators can simplify algebraic expressions symbolically (e.g. factoring \(x^2 - 9\) into \((x-3)(x+3)\) or taking symbolic derivatives \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin(x) = \cos(x)\)). StackCalc does not feature a CAS. Its solvers evaluate strictly numerical roots (via secant/Brent numerical methods) and numerical integrals (via Romberg quadrature), identical to classic approved scientific calculators.

  3. Standard Scientific Keypad: The keypad contains 43 tactile keys arranged in an industry-standard scientific matrix with numerical and transcendental legends. Keys do not follow typewriter (QWERTY) arrangements.

  4. Continuous Memory Reset Protocol: Before entering an exam center, test proctors can request students clear continuous memory. To clear all memory in seconds:

  5. Press Left Shift + C (CLEAR).
  6. Press CLSTK to purge all 4 operational stack levels (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  7. Press CLREGS to purge all 26 storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)).
  8. Press CLSTAT to purge statistical accumulations.

docs.title: 4. Frequently Asked Questions by Exam Proctors
docs.text:
Is Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) allowed on the SAT or ACT?

Yes. Neither The College Board nor ACT prohibits Reverse Polish Notation. Both organizations regulate calculator capabilities (disallowing QWERTY keyboards, wireless communication, and symbolic CAS), not the internal stack entry logic. RPN calculators have been officially permitted on collegiate and secondary exams for over 45 years.

Can students store formulas in continuous memory?

The SC-32 includes 26 general-purpose numerical storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)) for intermediate floating-point numbers. It does not possess a text editor, notes app, or file storage system. Proctors can verify a clean state by having students execute the CLEAR → CLREGS routine upon entering the examination hall.

Does the calculator have a sound or audio beeper that could distract other examinees?

No. The SC-32 contains no speaker, buzzer, or piezo element. Keystrokes are quiet mechanical tactile clicks (tactile microswitch actuation under flexible TPU keys).

docs.title: Embedded Swift firmware
docs.text:
StackCalc's firmware source targets the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 / RP2350 using Embedded Swift and a C hardware layer. It shares calculator logic and the bitmap interface with RPNCore.

The pictured physical calculator is an unpowered mechanical prototype. Board fabrication and integration are still in progress. The architecture below describes the current source, not measured performance of an assembled product. The public mechanical download does not include firmware source or a flashable release.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Source component Responsibility Main.swift Calculator event loop, input dispatch, display updates and continuous memory hardware_wrapper.c / BridgingHeader.h Pico SDK boundary for GPIO, SPI, time and flash RPNCore Shared calculator operations, key mapping, bitmap rendering and tutorials CMakeLists.txt Embedded build configuration; excludes app-only plotting Simulator/ Browser display and transport around the emulated firmware image

The physical design uses the current 37-key layout. Source sharing supports consistent behavior, but cross-platform parity must be checked with matching operations and state; it is not a blanket bit-for-bit guarantee for every feature.

docs.title: Display and input
docs.text:
The logical display is 132×65 pixels, with 1,188 bytes arranged as nine pages of 132 columns. The final page has one visible row. The hardware wrapper currently configures 8 MHz SPI and sends each page with blocking writes. It does not implement the previously described DMA or establish a tear-free display claim. Module/controller identity and physical edge visibility still need checking against the installed specimen and BOM.

The GPIO scanner samples the matrix; the Swift loop debounces changed input before dispatching the corresponding operation. The active loop uses a 10 ms sleep interval. In the source's sleeping state, the LCD output is disabled, scanning is restricted to C/ON, and the loop uses a 100 ms interval. Other keys do not wake that state. These source intervals are not measured touch-to-display latency or battery-life results.

docs.title: Continuous memory
docs.text:
The flash implementation alternates between two slots, each eight flash sectors, at the end of flash. It validates payloads with an FNV-1a checksum and selects the newer valid sequence. It also includes migration from the older, smaller slot layout.

This replaces the earlier description of two 4 KB sectors and CRC32. Power-loss recovery, flash endurance and retention must be evaluated on the matching board. The firmware uses allocated buffers and Swift collections; zero heap allocation is not a current claim.

docs.title: Build and inspection
docs.text:
These commands are for a source checkout with the configured Embedded Swift toolchain, Pico SDK, ARM compiler, CMake and Ninja. The current local Pico SDK checkout is based on 2.3.0. The build script accepts WATCHCALC_SWIFT_TOOLCHAIN for an external Swift toolchain and otherwise uses Firmware/toolchains/swift.

Run from the repository root:

# Hardware UF2
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh hardware

# Instrumented hardware build
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh profile

# Firmware image for the localhost emulator
Firmware/compile_firmware.sh emulator
node Firmware/Simulator/server.js

# ELF sizing and optional live hardware counters
python3 Firmware/profile_power_memory.py

Each build replaces Firmware/build; run the variants sequentially. The hardware output is Firmware/build/WatchCalcFirmware.uf2, copied to Hardware/output/WatchCalc32_Manufacturing/Firmware_Files/WatchCalcFirmware_RP2350.uf2. The profile variant uses the _Profile.uf2 suffix in that export directory. An emulator build is for the simulator, not for flashing a board.

docs.title: Physical verification still required
docs.text:
A powered board is needed to verify cold startup, input-to-display timing, display edges, memory recovery, current consumption and battery life. The previous sub-15 ms boot, sub-two-second flashing and multi-month battery statements were not qualified measurements and are withdrawn.

When a board-specific firmware release is available, its instructions must identify the board revision, matching UF2, USB/BOOTSEL access and recovery procedure. Do not infer those details from the mechanical prototype photos.

See the hardware build and capability reference for the current mechanical kit and its qualification limits.

docs.text: Dry-fit the matching faceplate and membrane in the chassis rails, then fit the snap-retained cap. Once the board arrives, the integration sequence will add board seating, display alignment, switch reach, connector clearance, battery polarity, and power checks. Release the retention features rather than prying on the display surround when reopening the printed assembly.

docs.text:

All physical StackCalc production handhelds (SC-32 and SC-6) are molded and printed in dark, technical, high-rigidity thermoplastics (Sunlu Midnight Navy PLA 2.0+, Technical Matte Black PLA/PETG, Elegoo Space Gray PLA, Sunlu Dark Chestnut PLA, and Sunlu Coffee Brown PLA).

docs.text:
These digital twin themes celebrate historical calculator designs within the iOS and iPadOS companion applications: * RetroFuturism (Virtual Only): Dieter Rams / 1980s Braun aerospace cream (#F5F5F3) with deep navy markings (#142240) and antique bronze accents (#784408). * Pioneer Brown (Virtual Only): 1988 Corvallis HP-32SII tribute in matte brown (#2E241C) with golden amber and cyan pad-printed legends. * Pioneer Black (Virtual Only): 1990s updated Pioneer release in deep matte black (#1F1F21) with emerald green and orchid purple legends.

Primary and secondary buttons share the same material. Button trenches are laser engraved and faceplate labels use 1064nm pulsed infrared laser foaming. Software colors communicate appearance; exact physical matches and abrasion resistance require specimen measurement. Orange/blue functional coding belongs exclusively to the fixed watch interface, including watch widgets. Filament base colors and manufacturing layer colors are separate.

docs.title: Print-in-place spring exploration
docs.text:
Before selecting the current TPU membrane direction, we printed integrated spring and key experiments to study travel, return behavior, and print tolerance in a single part. These experiments informed the mechanical layout, but they are not the current keypad design or a validation of final key force.

A printed test array with integrated circular key and spring features. It records an exploratory route that was superseded by the current TPU membrane direction.

Close view of the printed spring geometry. The current design work uses a separate TPU membrane; repeatable force, life, and tactile measurements remain future test work.

docs.title: 2. Classic Scientific RPN Parity & Modern Capability Rubric
docs.text: This rubric tracks operational capabilities across all StackCalc surfaces compared against classic scientific RPN handheld baselines. Capabilities below are implementation references; release claims require platform-specific regression and device evidence.

docs.title: 3. Deliberate Quality-of-Life Departures from Classic Handhelds
docs.text:
While maintaining functional pedigree, StackCalc incorporates deliberate modern enhancements to improve usability, durability, and educational clarity:

  1. Unified RPN Programming:
  2. Classic Handhelds: Required users to navigate between an archaic algebraic equation mode and keystroke programming.
  3. StackCalc: Unifies all equation definition into deterministic RPN stack operations. This eliminates parser ambiguities and ensures identical execution behavior on microcontrollers, phones, and watches.
  4. Dedicated Absolute Value (|x|) Key:
  5. Classic Handhelds: Hid the absolute value function deep within secondary menus.
  6. StackCalc: Assigns |x| directly to Right Shift +/-, providing instant one-touch evaluation.
  7. Modern Remainder Notation (÷R):
  8. Classic Handhelds: Labeled integer division ambiguously as INT÷.
  9. StackCalc: Uses ÷R to clearly communicate integer division with remainder, aligning with modern engineering and educational standards.
  10. Integrated Basic Plotting Engine (PLOT):
  11. Classic Handhelds: Required bulky peripheral thermal printers or external plotters to visualize data.
  12. StackCalc: Built-in plotting engine renders function evaluation curves (\(y = f(x)\)) and statistical scatter/regression plots directly on the transflective graphic LCD display and mobile screens.
  13. Clean Power Architecture (Software Targets):
  14. Classic Handhelds: Included a physical OFF key label.
  15. StackCalc: Retains power management on the hardware unit, but hides unnecessary power buttons on iOS and watchOS where operating system lifecycle handlers manage state.
  16. Configurable Stack Depth:
  17. Classic Handhelds: Restricted permanently to a 4-level stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  18. StackCalc: The FLAGS menu allows selecting between classic 4-level, 8-level, and unbounded Infinite stack depths.

docs.title: Apple Ecosystem & Desktop App: Mac, iPad, iPhone & Watch
docs.text:
StackCalc is engineered from day one as a unified physical-digital system. Our companion applications for macOS, iPadOS, iOS, and watchOS share the exact same deterministic Swift package—RPNCore—as our bare-metal Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller firmware.

The apps share calculator semantics through RPNCore; platform capabilities and completed native regression evidence determine supported behavior.

docs.title: 1. Apple Watch: Pitch-Black Rapid Field
docs.text:
The watchOS application is designed for instant, glanceable number crunching directly on your wrist:

  • True OLED #000000 Background: Preserves battery life and blends invisibly with Apple Watch Series 10/11 edges.
  • Edge-Glow Wayfinding Beacons: Directional boundary pulses (Burnt Orange on the left, Blue on the right, Cyan on top) guide your finger across the keypad without looking.
  • Macro Screen-Tap ENTER: Tap anywhere on the upper display to execute an instant stack-lift ENTER without targeting a tiny button.
  • Continuous Tactile Feedback: Powered by Apple's Taptic Engine to simulate physical tactile switches.

docs.title: 2. iPhone & iPad: The 10-Column Landscape Layout
docs.text:
On iPad and iPhone, StackCalc expands into a spacious landscape and portrait instrument inspired by classic 1980s landscape scientific computing layouts:

  • 12-Character Segmented LCD: Emulates the authentic EastRising ST7567 transflective display with bundled Terminus typography.
  • Continuous Tactile Field (HPTC): Zero-distance drag gestures let you slide across key seams with subtle boundary clicks, sinking into button centers for heavy mechanical actuations.
  • Expandable TUI Overlays: Complex operations like Plotting, Integration, Equation Editing, and Tutorials smoothly expand into an authentic Text User Interface terminal.

docs.title: 3. macOS Desktop App: Physical Keyboard Ergonomics & Multi-Register Studio
docs.text:
On Mac, StackCalc becomes an indispensable engineering workstation instrument for macOS:

  • Native macOS Binary: Universal build optimized for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) and Intel Macs, launching with zero startup latency.
  • Physical Keyboard & Numpad Mapping: Full physical keyboard ergonomics. The numeric keypad Enter executes RPN stack commit, standard arithmetic keys (+, -, *, /) trigger operations, Space or Return lifts the stack, and arrow keys cycle through registers.
  • Side-by-Side Multi-Register Inspector: On desktop monitors, expand the auxiliary side panel to inspect all operational stack levels (\(X, Y, Z, T\)), global storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)), and statistical accumulation registers (\(\Sigma\)) simultaneously.
  • Menu Bar Quick Calculator: Global keyboard shortcut summons a lightweight RPN scratchpad directly from the macOS menu bar for rapid calculations while writing code or LaTeX documents.

docs.title: 5. Widget Architecture & Tutorial Integration
docs.text:
Watch uses one fixed black/orange/cyan functional scheme. iPhone, iPad and their widgets use the chosen material palette with direction and shape to identify shifts. System widget tint may override app colors. Ordinary widget arithmetic remains available beyond five taps; native pending feedback and an Open calculator route support handoff. Visible latency depends on the host and must be measured; no zero-latency guarantee is made.

Tutorials retain the phone calculator geometry. Watch guidance uses full-screen pages followed by its normal keypad. SC6 retains the tested vertical X/T display and correction behavior; a horizontal operand layout is not the current implementation.

StackCalc Calculator is a tactile, deterministic scientific RPN calculator and visual K–8 math companion for iPhone, iPad, and a 100% standalone Apple Watch app.

docs.title: 2. The Founding Story & Vision: A Kid-Friendly Calculator That Grows With Them
docs.text:
Traditional math tools force learners through three disconnected worlds: children begin with physical classroom blocks, transition to algebraic school calculators cluttered with nested parentheses and syntax errors, and only encounter clean stack-based computation (Reverse Polish Notation) in university or professional engineering—often on discontinued vintage hardware like the HP-32SII (fetching $200+ on eBay with aging switches) or $250+ boutique collectors' calculators (such as the SwissMicros DM42/C47, DM32, DM41CC, or DM15CC).

After training our own children on a DM41CC—proving that kids master RPN effortlessly when freed from parenthesis soup—we realized two things: first, on a stack-based postfix calculator, users learn operator-precedence parsing themselves in order to decompose and enter expressions onto the visible stack—building real structural understanding and appreciating the lessons learned in the past 50 years of computing so they can build the next 50 years. Second, no parent wants a child carrying a $250 collector's instrument or a fragile $200 eBay antique to school every day. StackCalc was created to deliver a durable, kid-friendly RPN ecosystem—launching our initial small-batch maker hardware at $89.99 while engineering our volume manufacturing roadmap toward a $29.99 classroom target:

  • Why the HP-32SII Architecture Over the HP-15C or HP-42S: Rather than burying everyday operations inside deep hierarchical softkey menus (like the HP-42S) or requiring memorized numeric matrix/label codes on a landscape chassis (like the HP-15C), StackCalc builds on the HP-32SII's ergonomic sweet spot—keeping essential scientific operations directly accessible on the keys while using a clean 1-line context bar for CLEAR, STAT, SOLVE, and INTG.
  • Not an Emulator—A Clean-Room Engine with Modern Upgrades: Written from scratch in Swift (RPNCore) rather than wrapping vintage ROM dumps, StackCalc 32 adds Harmonic Mean (H.M.), Time Value of Money (TVM), a Quadratic & Cubic Polynomial Root Solver (POLY), and interactive curve plotting (PLOT), while StackCalc 6 covers Common Core math up through 6th grade with step-by-step prime-factor fraction simplification ([SIMP]), integer division with remainder (÷R), [PRIME], [GCD], and [LCM].
  • Even in the Age of AI, Students Need Mathematical Intuition: Handing a student a black-box LLM or an infix calculator that hides intermediate steps behind = undermines number sense. StackCalc pairs a visible operational stack with physical 3D-printed blocks (84mm Fraction Studio Towers and Logarithmic Prime Factor Slide Rules) and unit-test-verified workbooks from 1st grade (StackCalc 6) through AP Calculus (StackCalc 32).
  • Designed to Be Allowed in Testing Situations (No CAS Ban): Because CAS (Computer Algebra System) calculators are banned on the SAT, ACT, IB, UIL, NCEES FE/PE engineering exams, and most university math exams, StackCalc is purposefully designed for exam integrity—free of CAS symbolic engines, QWERTY keyboards, wireless transceivers, ads, or subscriptions.

docs.title: 3. One Unified App, Two Built-In Modes
docs.text: StackCalc is a single universal app that adapts to the user's stage of learning through two purpose-built modes:

docs.title: Mode A: Scientific Mode (StackCalc 32) — The Modern HP-32SII Reimagined
docs.text:
Designed for engineers, scientists, AP students, and anyone who values speed and transparency over black-box answers:

  • Zero Parentheses, Visible 4-Level Stack (X, Y, Z, T): Enter numbers, tap operations, and watch intermediate results stay visible at every step. You never lose your place or battle syntax errors.
  • Exact Mixed Fractions (a b/c): Rapid dot-separated fraction entry (e.g., .1.2 for \(\frac{1}{2}\) or 2.1.8 for \(2\frac{1}{8}\)) and exact rational arithmetic (FDISP) without floating-point rounding drift.
  • Multi-Variable Equation Solver, TVM & Polynomials: Store custom formulas, solve numerically for any unknown variable, run 5-variable Time Value of Money (TVM) and Quadratic/Cubic Polynomial (POLY) solvers, and evaluate definite integrals using Simpson convergence.
  • Interactive Curve Plotting: High-contrast graphing canvas with real-time root inspection, inflection tracing, and shaded area-under-the-curve integration.
  • STEM & Computer Science Toolkit: Complex numbers, 2-variable statistical regressions (including Harmonic Mean H.M.), and Base-N programmer modes (HEX, DEC, OCT, BIN).

docs.title: The Big Picture: Why We Are Building StackCalc
docs.text:
If you ask a classroom of elementary or middle school students how they feel about math, far too many will say: "I'm just not a math person."

Why does this happen? Because traditional education rushes children into abstract alphanumeric symbols (\(x + y = z\)) and flat 2D worksheets long before their brains have developed intuitive, spatial number sense. Then, in high school, we hand them complex black-box calculators with hidden menus and arbitrary syntax rules.

StackCalc was founded to change this from the ground up.

We are an open-source engineering initiative reimagining how human beings learn mathematics: - We believe mathematics is tactile, physical, and intuitive. - You should be able to touch place value. You should be able to feel a common denominator. You should be able to see a prime number stand alone. - Our ecosystem spans from concrete 3D-printed blocks for kindergarteners, all the way to open-source hardware handheld scientific calculators (the SC-6 and SC-32) that students build, program, and understand from the silicon up.

Whether you only print a single kit for your child's homework desk or build the full open-hardware calculator, you are giving a student the superpower of physical mathematical intuition.

docs.title: Why 3D Printing & Open Hardware: The Hybrid Model
docs.text:
Commercial manipulative kits from educational publishers cost $40 to $80 per box. They are sold in closed corporate ecosystems, and when two unit blocks roll under a radiator or get lost in a backpack, the whole set is ruined and ends up abandoned in a classroom closet.

We chose an open-source hybrid model:

  1. Free to 3D Print (Open Source): If you or your school have a 3D printer, every single component, tray, and block is free to download and print right here on Printables under a Creative Commons (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) license. No digital paywalls, no subscriptions.
  2. "No Lost Piece Left Behind": Every single part carries a permanent, debossed Part ID matching the included inventory card. If a block goes missing, don't throw away the set—just download that single Part ID STL and print an exact replacement in 15–20 minutes!
  3. Don't Have a 3D Printer? We've Got You Covered: For parents, schools, and teachers who don't have access to 3D printers, we manufacture and sell finished physical kits. You can order on-demand factory refills directly through our Slant 3D Portal, or handcrafted boxed sets with printed cards and spiral guides from our Etsy Storefront.
  4. Engineered for Real Classrooms: Zero supports, zero fragile filament swaps, and heavy-duty 3-perimeter walls designed to survive tile floor drops.

docs.title: Storage Architecture: Gridfinity, Snapfinity & Quarter-Gridfinity (21 mm)
docs.text:
Every StackCalc manipulative kit is engineered from the ground up to eliminate classroom clutter, prevent lost parts, and enable cross-kit physical arithmetic through three architectural principles:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  STACKCALC MODULAR HARDWARE ARCHITECTURE                |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| 42 mm Standard Gridfinity Pitch    | Snapfinity Dual-Purpose Lids       |
| • Open standard storage envelope   | • Secure friction fit for travel   |
| • Stacks in drawer grids & carts   | • Inverts into calculation stage   |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| Quarter-Gridfinity (21 mm)         | Cross-Kit Interchangeability       |
| • 19 mm MathBlock + clearance      | • Digit blocks fit Ten-Frames      |
| • Exactly 4 blocks per 42 mm cell  | • Array tiles fit Algebra Studio   |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
  1. Gridfinity Standard (42 mm Pitch): Every storage bin, caddy, and display stand adheres strictly to Zach Freedman's open 42 mm Gridfinity specification. Bins nest securely into standard classroom organizers, drawer matrices, and rolling makerspace carts.
  2. Snapfinity Dual-Purpose Lids & Stages: Our lids do double duty. Snapped on top of a bin, they provide child-resistant friction retention for transport. Flipped over onto a student's desk, they become structured calculation stages and alignment workbenches with calibrated detents for physical problem-solving.
  3. Quarter-Gridfinity Sub-Grid (21 mm Pitch): StackCalc MathBlocks are sized on a 21 mm modular quarter-grid (19 mm block footprint + calibrated clearance). This allows exactly 4 MathBlocks to dock into any standard 42 mm Gridfinity cell (a 2x2 matrix), creating a dense, space-efficient classroom footprint.
  4. Cross-Kit Interchangeability: Blocks, tokens, and trays are universal across the entire ecosystem. Place Value digit blocks drop directly into Ten-Frame arithmetic trays; Counting Tiles interface seamlessly with Algebra Factoring rails; and both SC-32 and SC-6 handheld calculators dock side-by-side with your manipulative trays using the Modular Desk Stand.

docs.title: From Blocks to the Stack: The CPA Learning Continuum & RPN
docs.text:
Why do our manipulatives mention calculators and "stacks"?

When children learn math with physical blocks, they stack them vertically. When computer scientists and engineers calculate, they use an operational stack (Reverse Polish Notation, or RPN)—the exact same stack-based logic pioneered by Hewlett-Packard and modern computer architectures.

StackCalc implements Jerome Bruner's Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract (CPA) pedagogical framework: - 1. Concrete: Students handle tactile, physical blocks with calibrated heights, weights, and socket detents. - 2. Pictorial: Students organize blocks into visible visual arrangements (arrays, fraction bars, ten-frames, and factoring rectangles). - 3. Abstract: Students translate their physical proofs directly into numbers, equations, and calculator operations.

docs.title: Bridging Manipulatives to Reverse Polish Notation (RPN)
docs.text: Traditional algebraic calculators hide intermediate numbers behind an invisible parenthesis hierarchy. StackCalc couples physical manipulatives directly with Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) stack computing: - Stacking physical blocks vertically mirrors pushing values onto the calculator's operational stack (X, Y, Z, and T registers). - Performing a physical operation (combining two towers or regrouping a ten-frame) mirrors executing an RPN operator key ([+], [x], [ENTER]). - Designed as the physical companion to the SC-6 Elementary Calculator (featuring dedicated non-shifted keys like [PV], [FDISP], [SIMP], [PRIME], and [?]), our 120 station worksheets, and our illustrated companion textbook on Amazon: From Blocks to the Stack: The RPN Journey (ASIN B0HPJN3KP9).

docs.text:
StackCalc MathBlocks are engineered specifically for clean, reliable printing on standard single-extruder 3D printers:

  1. 1.2 mm Deep Debossed Numerals & Symbols: All digits, fractions, and legends are recessed 1.2 mm into the top and side surfaces.   4. Geometric Meaning: In StackCalc mathematics, place value and mathematical meaning are derived from position and geometry (quarter-grid slots and stages), not artificial color coding. Any spool of standard PLA in your maker space will produce a 100% mathematically valid, fully functional kit.

docs.text:

  • Single-Command Batch Generation: Each kit includes a POSIX Makefile that compiles individual modular parts or consolidated, color-separated production plates matching our commercial print farm specifications:

cd 02_fraction_studio_towers

# 1. Compile color-coded Slant 3D farm production plates
make plates

# 2. Compile individual modular component STLs
make parts

# 3. Clean generated build outputs
make clean

docs.title: 1. Place Value Studio & Regrouping Trays (PLACE-01)
docs.text: Grades 1–5 • Base-Ten Positional Notation, Multi-Digit Addition/Subtraction, Regrouping/Carrying, Decimals

docs.title: Why Your Kids Need This Kit
docs.text: Place value is the single most critical foundation of elementary mathematics—and the #1 reason kids develop early math anxiety. When children see a number like 342, their brains initially perceive three separate, equal digits rather than 3 hundreds, 4 tens, and 2 ones. When multi-digit addition and subtraction introduce 'carrying' and 'borrowing' (regrouping), abstract pencil-and-paper scratch marks feel like arbitrary black magic. When decimals arrive, kids frequently believe 0.05 is larger than 0.2 simply because '5 is bigger than 2.' They desperately need to hold place value in their physical hands.

docs.title: How It Works in Practice
docs.text:
The Place Value Studio makes positional notation physical through dual 6x2 activity trays: one dedicated to Whole Numbers (100k down to 1) and one dedicated to Decimals (0.1 down to 0.000001). Digit blocks sit in quarter-grid sockets. When students add 7 + 8, they place seven and eight blocks in the ones column, immediately see the slot overflow past 10, and physically exchange ten ones for an interlocking +1 regrouping carry token that snaps into the tens column. Because both the digit blocks and the +1 carry tokens share the exact same 19.0 x 19.0 x 8.85 mm dimensions (7.0 mm visible stack height) and identical 1.85 mm stacking sockets, they align to the exact same waterline across all tray channels and stack vertically with zero wobble. Across the decimal boundary, the physical separation cements that tenths, hundredths, and thousandths are diminishing fractional subdivisions, making decimal arithmetic visual and intuitive.

3X1X7U GRIDFINITY • HARDWARE KEY: [PV] Includes Whole Tray, Decimal Tray, 44 Symmetric Digit Tiles (22 White + 22 Blue-Gray), 4 Regrouping (+1) Tokens, 7U Box with 12 Labeled Floor Sockets, and Snapfinity Stage Lid. DOWNLOAD 3MF ↗ SPECS & LESSONS → ORDER ON ETSY ↗ REFILLS ON SLANT 3D ↗

docs.title: 2. Fraction Studio Proportional Towers (FRAC-01)
docs.text: Grades 3–8 • Proportional Equivalence, Common Denominators, Fraction Reduction, Mixed Numbers, Decimals & Percentages

docs.title: Why Your Kids Need This Kit
docs.text: Ask any fourth or fifth grader which is larger: 1/3 or 1/8. A shocking number of students will say 1/8 because their brains have spent years learning that '8 is bigger than 3.' Traditional 2D pie charts on worksheets fail because comparing curved pizza wedges is visually ambiguous and prone to optical illusion. Kids need a linear, proportional physical proof where mathematical equality is undeniable.

docs.title: How It Works in Practice
docs.text:
Every tower's height is mathematically calibrated: \(h = 84/d\text{ mm}\), where \(d\) is the denominator. The 1 Whole tower is exactly \(84.0\text{ mm}\) tall (2 Gridfinity units). The Half tower is \(42.0\text{ mm}\). The Third tower is \(28.0\text{ mm}\), the Fourth tower is \(21.0\text{ mm}\), and the Twelfth tower is exactly \(7.0\text{ mm}\) (identically matching the 7.0 mm visible height of our Place Value blocks!). docs.title: 3. Prime Factor Studio & Slide Rule Comparator (PRIME-01)
docs.text: Grades 3–9 • Prime Factorization, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, LCM, GCD, Logarithmic Stacking

docs.title: Why Your Kids Need This Kit
docs.text: Prime numbers are the fundamental 'atoms' of mathematics, yet in traditional school curricula, prime factorization is reduced to tedious, repetitive 'factor trees' drawn in pencil. Students memorize that 2, 3, 5, and 7 are prime, but they have zero intuition for why prime decomposition powers modern cryptography, how LCM and GCD work geometrically, or what the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic actually guarantees.

docs.title: How It Works in Practice
docs.text:
The Prime Factor Studio is the world's first logarithmic manipulative where stacking primes physically multiplies them. Tower heights follow the logarithmic scaling function \(h(p) = k \cdot \ln(p)\). Because logarithms convert multiplication into addition (\(\ln(a \times b) = \ln(a) + \ln(b)\)), when you stack the [2] block (\(24.0\text{ mm}\)) on top of the [3] block (\(38.0\text{ mm}\)), their combined height is exactly \(62.0\text{ mm}\)—which precisely aligns with the composite [6] benchmark on the bilateral slide rule comparator! Stacking [2], [2], and [3] physically reaches [12]. To find the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of two numbers, students simply compare their prime towers and find the shared physical height.

docs.title: Why Your Kids Need This Kit
docs.text: Before a young child can add or subtract, they must develop subitizing—the cognitive ability to recognize a quantity of objects instantly without counting 1, 2, 3... one by one. If children rely on counting fingers or pencil tallies, they hit a cognitive wall as soon as numbers exceed 10. They need a visual and tactile framework that anchors all arithmetic to the benchmark number 10.

docs.title: How It Works in Practice
docs.text:
The Ten-Frame Studio uses two modular 2x5 recessed grid stages and 40 tactile debossed counters. Arranging counters into the 2x5 grid instantly reveals combinations to 10: a student sees a full row of 5 plus 2 more and immediately recognizes \(5 + 2 = 7\), noticing the 3 empty spots that prove \(10 - 7 = 3\). When bridging across 10 (e.g. \(8 + 5\)), the student fills the two empty spots on the first frame to 'make 10', and leaves 3 on the second frame, making \(8 + 5 = 10 + 3 = 13\) visual and effortless. All 10 counters slide into the elevated Carry Shelf, where the solid 2U Carry Cube cements the transition from loose units into a solid ten.

100 precision interlocking tiles nest into a chamfered 10x10 staging tray with tactile perimeter guide marks. Building \(4 \times 6\) means laying out 4 rows of 6 tiles (\(24\) tiles total). docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
// LEGAL PROTOCOL · ZERO DATA COLLECTION · EFFECTIVE SEPTEMBER 14, 2026

At StackCalc, we believe mathematics is personal, foundational, and should never be accompanied by surveillance, telemetry, or advertising. Whether you are using StackCalc32 on iOS, iPadOS, or Apple Watch, or following the physical calculator project, we collect zero personal data.

docs.title: 1. Zero Data Collection
docs.text:
• No Personal Information: We do not collect names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, or any personally identifiable information (PII).
  • No Analytics or Telemetry: We do not track keystrokes, calculation frequency, app session length, feature adoption, or user workflows.
  • No Device Identifiers: We do not read or transmit IDFA (Identifier for Advertisers), IDFV (Identifier for Vendors), MAC addresses, or IP addresses.
  • No Diagnostics or Crash Reports: We do not bundle third-party crash tracking or diagnostic SDKs.
  • No Biometrics or Health Data: While running standalone on Apple Watch, StackCalc does not access Apple Health, heart rate sensors, workout data, or any biometric sensors.

docs.title: 2. 100% Local On-Device Computation
docs.text:
Every calculation, stack operation, variable memory register, equation, and statistical curve is evaluated exclusively within the local memory of your device:

  • RPN Stack & Memory Registers: Stack levels (X, Y, Z, T, and extended levels), storage registers (0–9, A–Z), and financial registers are stored in local device memory only.
  • Continuous Memory: In accordance with physical calculator behavior, values stored in continuous memory remain preserved locally between app sessions until manually cleared (CLEAR → Continuous Memory) or until the application is removed from your device.
  • No Cloud Synchronization: The application operates completely offline. No network connectivity is required, requested, or used.

docs.title: 3. Third-Party Services & SDKs
docs.text: The application contains zero third-party software development kits (SDKs), tracking pixels, ad networks, or third-party APIs. We do not sell, rent, monetize, or disclose any user data to third parties under any circumstance.

docs.title: 4. Children’s Online Privacy Protection (COPPA & Global Standards)
docs.text:
StackCalc is designed for learners of all ages, from elementary school students exploring exact fraction manipulatives to university students and professionals performing advanced scientific analysis.

  • Because we do not collect any personal data from any user, we strictly comply with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and California privacy laws.
  • We do not require account creation, registration, or login.
  • Children can safely use StackCalc in classrooms, exams, and at home without privacy risk.

docs.title: 5. Website Privacy (stackcalc.io)
docs.text:
Our documentation and storefront website (https://www.stackcalc.io) is hosted via GitHub Pages. Standard server access logs (such as IP addresses and browser user-agent headers) may be automatically processed by GitHub to ensure infrastructure security and deliver the web service. We do not inject tracking cookies or third-party marketing trackers on this documentation site.

StackCalc does not currently process direct physical-product purchases through this website. If a future product links to a named marketplace, that marketplace's privacy policy will describe its checkout, payment, and shipping-data practices.

docs.title: 6. Data Retention and Deletion
docs.text:
Because StackCalc collects no data on remote servers:

  • There is no remote account or database record to delete.
  • To erase all local state, press Yellow Shift + C (CLEAR) → tap CLALL inside the app, or uninstall the application from your Apple device.

docs.title: 7. Changes to This Policy
docs.text: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect future updates or legal compliance. Any changes will be posted immediately to this URL (https://www.stackcalc.io/privacy/) with an updated effective date.

docs.title: 8. Contact Information
docs.text:
If you have questions or inquiries regarding this Privacy Policy, please reach out through our public channels:

  • GitHub Issue Tracker: https://github.com/abagher2/stackcalc/issues
  • Web Support & Help Desk: https://www.stackcalc.io/support/
  • Documentation & public downloads: https://www.stackcalc.io

docs.text: Dimension Specification Engineering Justification Width \(135.0\,\text{mm}\) Fits within \(150\,\text{mm} \times 150\,\text{mm}\) laser engraving working beds with \(7.5\,\text{mm}\) perimeter clamping margin. docs.title: Pathway A: High-Speed Laser Printer Paper (Bulk School District Orders)
docs.text:
• Target Orders: Classroom 10-packs, 30-packs, and school district purchase orders.
  • Substrate: 80 lb / 216 gsm bright white acid-free cardstock.
  • Toner Strategy: Clean white background (#FFFFFF) with high-contrast midnight charcoal typography (#0F172A).
  • Why avoid full black flood? Flooding paper with black toner causes thermal curl, ink flaking on folds, and smudge risk during humid classroom use.
  • Zero-Cut Feeding Solution: Feed pre-cut \(4 \times 6\text{ in}\) (\(101.6 \times 152.4\,\text{mm}\)) or \(3.5 \times 5\text{ in}\) (\(88.9 \times 127\,\text{mm}\)) blank index cardstock into the laser printer's manual bypass tray, completely eliminating manual scissors or paper trimmer labor.
  • Throughput: ~30 double-sided cards per minute.

docs.title: Pathway B: Precision Laser-Engraved Black Card (SC-32 & Retail Kits)
docs.text:
• Target Orders: SC-32 scientific calculator, keynote showcase editions, and direct retail.
  • Substrate: 300 gsm black matte cardstock (with white core) or \(1.0\,\text{mm}\) black anodized aluminum / black cast acrylic.
  • Color Constraint: Strictly Monochrome White on Black (#FFFFFF on #000000). Laser ablation vaporizes the black top coat to reveal crisp white substrate underneath.
  • Single-Pass Automation (Zero Manual Cutting):
  • The laser engraves the exploded wireframe, Part ID manifest, California QC badge, and Side B vector QR code.
  • In the same job without moving the substrate, the laser vector-cuts the outer \(135.0 \times 90.0\,\text{mm}\) boundary with \(r = 3.0\,\text{mm}\) rounded corners.
  • Finished, deburred cards drop out ready for packaging—zero manual labor.
  • Throughput: ~90 seconds per double-sided card.

docs.title: 1. How does RPN (Stack Math) work? Why are there no parentheses?
docs.text:
In Reverse Polish Notation (RPN), operators follow their operands: - To evaluate \(5 + 3\): Press 5, ENTER, 3, +. - To evaluate \((4 \times 5) + (6 \times 7)\): Press 4, ENTER, 5, ×, 6, ENTER, 7, ×, +.

RPN completely eliminates parentheses, eliminates syntax errors, and keeps all intermediate calculation steps visible in the 4-level stack (X, Y, Z, T).

docs.title: 2. How do I display and calculate with exact fractions?
docs.text: StackCalc includes an arbitrary-precision rational fractions engine: - To toggle between decimal representation and exact fractional notation, press Left Shift + . (FDISP). - A decimal like 2.125 instantly renders as exact 2 1/8. - Pressing . between integers enters mixed fractions directly (e.g., 3 . 1 /c 2 for \(3 \frac{1}{2}\)).

docs.title: 3. Does the Apple Watch app require an iPhone nearby?
docs.text: No. StackCalc for watchOS is a 100% standalone instrument. - The entire calculation engine runs locally on the watch's processor. - You can perform full 4-level stack calculations, statistical summations, and trigonometric analysis directly on your wrist with zero phone connectivity. - Features high-contrast typography, digital crown scrubbing, and continuous edge-glow tactile haptic pulses.

docs.title: 4. How do I switch between the Hardware Digital Twin and Modern App interfaces?
docs.text: StackCalc offers two distinct user interfaces on iPhone and iPad: - Hardware Replica (Default): An authentic, brutalist digital twin of our physical open-source hardware, featuring the high-contrast icy silver-blue ST7567A dot-matrix screen, trapezoidal tactile TPU key caps, and laser-marked legends. - Modern App: An expansive, glassmorphism-free touch interface with dynamic softkeys and high-resolution TUI graph rendering. - To Switch Interface: Press Left Shift + FLAGS (or tap FLAGS in the menu catalog) → HW → select APP or REPLICA. - Faceplate Themes: You can also customize faceplate aesthetics in the same menu via FLAGS → FACE (RETRO, STEALTH, NOVA, SPACE, or VOYAGER).

docs.title: 5. How do I use the Equation Solver and Numerical Integrator?
docs.text: StackCalc includes an equation solver based on classic Romberg numerical integration and secant root-finding algorithms: 1. Press Right Shift + STO (EQN Mode) to view or input equations. 2. Select an equation (such as the preloaded Normal PDF NPDF). 3. Press SOLVE to solve for any independent variable without isolating it algebraically. 4. Press ∫ (Integrate) to perform numerical integration across specified upper and lower bounds.

docs.title: 6. How do I clear continuous memory or reset the calculator?
docs.text:
• Clear Current X Entry / Cancel: Press C (or backspace ←).
  • The CLEAR Menu: Press Left Shift + C (CLEAR) to open the dedicated memory reset menu:
  • CLSTK: Clears all four levels of the operational stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).
  • CLREGS: Clears the 26 storage registers (\(R_0 \dots R_{25}\)).
  • CLSTAT: Clears all two-variable statistical accumulation registers (\(\Sigma x, \Sigma y, \Sigma x^2, \Sigma y^2, \Sigma xy, n\)).
  • CLEQN: Clears all stored user equations.
  • CLVARS: Clears all variables and financial registers.
  • CLALL: Complete factory reset; clears all stack levels, variables, registers, and equations back to initial state.

docs.title: Learn by Doing: Interactive TUI Tutorials
docs.text:
The StackCalc32 firmware, Apple Watch app, and iOS app include 16 built-in interactive lessons powered by the native Text User Interface (TUI).

The TUI replaces standard nested modal dialogues with an expandable, chatbot-style scrolling terminal rendered in the bundled Terminus pixel font. Lessons describe physical and digital calculator operations, providing real-time verification against the deterministic RPNCore engine.

docs.title: 1. Terminal Navigation & Controls
docs.text:
Learn how to navigate the expandable TUI scrolling transcript buffer and switch between the standard 1-line LCD and the full-screen terminal.

> TUI: CONTROLS (LESSON 1/16) [C] EXIT

> Terminal navigation tutorial.

> Use ↰ + 8 to scroll up and ↰ + 7 to scroll down.

> Step 1: Press Left Shift (↰)

> Step 2: Press 8 [SCROLL UP]

> Step 3: Press Left Shift (↰)

> Step 4: Press 7 [SCROLL DOWN]

> VERIFIED: Transcript buffer navigation unlocked.

0.0000_ [NEXT]
  • Tap ↰ (Left Shift) to engage the shift annunciator.
  • Tap 8 to scroll up into previous calculation history.
  • Tap 7 to scroll down back to the active prompt.
  • Tap C to dismiss the TUI overlay back to the primary stack view.

docs.title: 2. RPN Basics: Eliminating Parentheses
docs.text:
Reverse Polish Notation replaces the traditional = button and parenthesis keys with an automatic 4-level stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).

Mission: Calculate \(5 + 3\) without parentheses.

> TUI: RPN BASICS (LESSON 2/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Calculate 5 + 3 with no parentheses.

> In RPN, you enter arguments first, then specify the operator.

> Step 1: Tap 5

> Step 2: Tap ENTER [Lifts 5 into Stack Register Y]

> Step 3: Tap 3 [Enters 3 into Stack Register X]

> Step 4: Tap + [Combines Y and X into X]

> VERIFIED: X = 8.0000 [STACK LIFT ARMED]

8.0000_ [NEXT]
  1. Tap 5: Types 5_ left-justified on the LCD display.
  2. Tap ENTER: Commits 5 to the bottom of the stack and arms stack-lift.
  3. Tap 3: Types 3_ in the active \(X\) register while \(Y\) retains 5.
  4. Tap +: Instantly evaluates \(5 + 3 = 8.0000\).

docs.title: 3. Complex Numbers: Euler’s Identity
docs.text:
StackCalc handles full complex pairs \((a + bi)\) natively across all scientific and transcendental functions.

Mission: Verify Euler's identity: \(e^{\pi i} = -1\).

> TUI: COMPLEX PAIRS (LESSON 3/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Verify e^(πi) = −1 with complex pairs.

> Step 1: Tap 0 -> press ENTER [Real part in Y = 0]

> Step 2: Tap Right Shift -> Tap SIN (π) [Imaginary part in X = 3.1416]

> Step 3: Tap Left Shift -> Tap STO (CMPLX) [Arms complex operator]

> Step 4: Tap eˣ [Evaluates transcendental e^(0 + πi)]

> Step 5: Left Shift -> STO (CMPLX) -> Right Shift -> ENTER (SHOW)

> VERIFIED: Result = −1.0000 + 0.0000i

-1.0000_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 4. Fraction Entry & Manual Simplification ([SIMP])
docs.text:
Unlike consumer calculators that automatically simplify fractions and hide the underlying math from students, StackCalc preserves exact fraction state. Students must press [SIMP] to actively reduce fractions step-by-step.

Mission: Enter \(\frac{2}{4}\) and reduce it to \(\frac{1}{2}\).

> TUI: FRACTION SIMPLIFICATION (LESSON 5/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Enter 2/4 and reduce step-by-step.

> Format: [Whole] . [Numerator] . [Denominator]

> Step 1: Tap . -> Tap 2 -> Tap . -> Tap 4 [.2.4]

> Step 2: Tap ENTER [Displays: .2.4_ without reducing]

> Step 3: Tap Softkey [SIMP]

> VERIFIED: Common divisor 2 factored out -> .1.2 (.1/2)

.1.2_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 5. Mixed Fraction Arithmetic & Decimal Toggle ([FDISP])
docs.text:
Add mixed numbers exactly and toggle instantly between exact fractional form and floating-point decimal.

Mission: Add \(1 \frac{1}{2} + 1 \frac{3}{4} = 3 \frac{1}{4} = 3.2500\).

> TUI: MIXED FRACTION ARITHMETIC (LESSON 6/16) [C] EXIT

> Mission: Add 1 1/2 + 1 3/4 exactly.

> Step 1: Tap 1 . 1 . 2 -> Press ENTER [1 1/2 in Y]

> Step 2: Tap 1 . 3 . 4 [1 3/4 in X]

> Step 3: Tap + [Exact sum evaluated: 3 1/4]

> Step 4: Tap [FDISP] to toggle to decimal representation.

> VERIFIED: 3.2500 [PRESS FDISP AGAIN TO RETURN TO 3_1/4]

3.2500_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 6. Time Value of Money (TVM Amortization)
docs.text:
The built-in financial solver handles loan payments, mortgages, savings plans, and balloon notes without requiring complex algebraic formulas.

Mission: Calculate the monthly payment on a $200,000 30-year fixed loan at 5.5% annual interest.

\[\text{Monthly Payment} = \frac{PV \cdot i}{1 - (1 + i)^{-N}}\] > TUI: TVM AMORTIZATION (LESSON 8/16) [C] EXIT

> Loan parameters: N=360 months, I%YR=0.4583% (5.5% ÷ 12), PV=$200,000

> Step 1: 360 -> [N] (Number of periods)

> Step 2: 5.5 -> [ENTER] -> 12 -> [÷] -> [I%YR] (Monthly periodic rate)

> Step 3: 200000 -> [PV] (Present loan value)

> Step 4: 0 -> [FV] (Future loan balance)

> Step 5: Press [PMT] to execute solver.

> VERIFIED: PMT = -$1,135.58 / month

-1,135.58_ [NEXT]

docs.title: 7. Statistical Sums & Standard Deviation
docs.text:
Accumulate 2-variable data pairs \((x, y)\) into continuous memory registers using [Σ+] to calculate means and sample standard deviations.

Mission: Enter sample data points \((2, 4)\) and \((4, 6)\), then solve mean and standard deviation.

> TUI: STATISTICS & STD DEV (LESSON 14/16) [C] EXIT

> Step 1: Tap Left Shift (↰) -> CLEAR -> Σ (Clears stat registers)

> Step 2: 4 [Y] -> ENTER -> 2 [X] -> Tap Σ+ [Accumulates n=1]

> Step 3: 6 [Y] -> ENTER -> 4 [X] -> Tap Σ+ [Accumulates n=2]

> Step 4: Tap Right Shift -> yˣ (x̄, ȳ) -> Mean X = 3.0000, Mean Y = 5.0000

> Step 5: Tap Right Shift -> ¹/x (s, σ) -> Sample StdDev = 1.4142

> VERIFIED: Standard deviation s = 1.4142

1.4142_ [EXIT]

docs.title: 8. Executing Tutorials on Physical Firmware (RP2350)
docs.text: StackCalc32's 16 guided lessons are not limited to touchscreens—they are implemented natively in bare-metal Embedded Swift running on the physical RP2350 microcontroller. The hardware provides an authentic, distraction-free environment to master RPN calculation.

docs.title: Hardware Launch Sequence
docs.text:
• Dedicated Launcher Key: Press Left Shift ([↰]) + [C] anywhere on the physical keypad to launch the built-in Interactive Tutorial Runner.
  • Instant Event Interception: The firmware event loop intercepts matrix scanning, suspends the standard operational stack, and loads the active tutorial state machine directly into the display buffer.

docs.title: Physical Display & Dynamic Softkeys
docs.text:
• ST7567A Transflective LCD: The 132×65 pixel monochrome display renders a 4-line terminal transcript using the sharp 6×8 pixel Terminus font. High contrast ensures clear legibility in classroom and laboratory lighting without backlight glare.
  • Tactile Softkey Integration: The top row of 6 tactile keys dynamically maps to contextual controls:
  • Key 1 ([PREV]): Revisit the previous instruction step.
  • Key 2 ([NEXT]): Advance to the next step once target preconditions are verified.
  • Key 5 ([SKIP]): Jump ahead to the subsequent lesson in the curriculum.
  • Key 6 ([EXIT]): Dismiss the tutorial session and immediately restore your active calculation stack.

docs.title: Real-Time Keystroke & Stack Verification
docs.text:
• When an instructional step prompts for an input sequence (for example, 5 [ENTER] 3 [+]), the firmware monitors physical switch actuations across the 43-key matrix.
  • Each switch closure evaluates against the deterministic RPNCore math engine.
  • Upon matching expected results, the LCD displays VERIFIED: [TEST PASSED] and enables the [NEXT] softkey to advance.

docs.title: Non-Volatile Flash Memory Persistence
docs.text:
• Progress across the 16 lessons is tracked via an internal bitmask stored in the RP2350's non-volatile QSPI flash memory (firmwareTutorialCompletionMask).
  • Your tutorial progress and mastery state persist across deep sleep, power cycles, and battery changes.

Welcome to the StackCalc Learning Lab Curriculum Hub. At StackCalc, we believe that mathematical comprehension should not begin behind a flat pane of glass or inside abstract parentheses soup.

Our instructional system bridges Jerome Bruner’s Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA) framework with the mechanical clarity of Reverse Polish Notation (RPN): 1. Concrete: Students assemble, measure, and verify quantities on physical desk workbench lids. 2. Representational: Students diagram tape models, area grids, and number bonds in structured lab sheets. 3. Abstract: Students formalize the calculation on 4-line live operational stacks (SC-6 Elementary and SC-32 Scientific), where the physical drop and lift of numbers mirror physical reality.

docs.title: 4-Stack XYZT, Skip-Counting [REP], LastX Verification & Integer Division
docs.text:
RPN PEDAGOGY // ELEMENTARY FOUNDATIONS (GRADES K–6) ● DEFAULT 4-STACK XYZT • CLASSROOM PROVEN 📖 Master Guide 🧑‍🏫 Book 1: Teacher Guide 🎯 Standards Matrix 📝 Worksheets ⚡ RPN Power Guide 🏆 UIL Competition 📥 Student Workbooks (.PDF) 🛒 Print Books (Amazon) ↗

Traditional elementary calculators force children into an algebraic syntax that creates unnecessary cognitive barriers: students struggle with hidden memory registers (M+), syntax errors caused by nested parentheses, and decimal answers when they are learning division with remainders.

In the latest system revisions, the StackCalc SC-6 Elementary Calculator standardizes on a default 4-stack XYZT live operational display for general arithmetic, while providing a toggleable 2-stack mode (\(Y, X\)) for early elementary instruction when focusing on two-row Place Value trays (PLACE-01). This guide explains the mathematical and pedagogical rationale behind this architecture, and provides classroom-ready teaching modules for core RPN elementary capabilities:

  1. The 4-Stack XYZT Visual Model & 2-Stack Manipulative Modes: Visual permanence for multi-step arithmetic, with focused 2-line views for paired entry.
  2. Integer Division with Remainders ([÷R]): Simultaneous quotient (\(X\)) and remainder (\(Y\)) display.
  3. Instant Inverse Verification ([LASTX]): Concrete student self-checking without teacher intervention.
  4. Rhythmic Skip-Counting ([REP]): Auditory and tactile reinforcement of multiplication facts.

docs.title: 1. Why 4-Stack XYZT is the Default in Elementary Math
docs.text:
In early prototype testing, a 2-line display was considered for simplicity. However, empirical classroom trials across Grades 3–6 revealed that a 4-level XYZT stack is dramatically more intuitive for young learners for three fundamental reasons:

+-------------------------------------------------------+
|  HIGH-CONTRAST MONOCHROME LCD (TERMINUS PIXEL FONT)   |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
|  T:        12.0000   <-- Top / Overflow Memory Level  |
|  Z:        35.0000   <-- Suspended Subtotal Level     |
|  Y:         3.0000   <-- Active Remainder / Operand 1 |
|  X:         5.0000   <-- Active Input / Quotient      |
+-------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 1.1 Cognitive Load & Visual Permanence
docs.text:
On a standard calculator, intermediate calculations vanish. In a problem like: $\((4 \times 8) + (15 \div 3)\)$ a student evaluating \(4 \times 8 = 32\) must either write \(32\) down on scratch paper, memorize it in short-term memory, or master obscure memory keys (STO, RCL, M+).

On the SC-6, evaluating 4 [ENTER] 8 [×] leaves 32 sitting visibly in the stack. When the student types 15 [ENTER] 3 [÷], 32 gently slides up to Register \(Y\), while 5 appears in Register \(X\). Both numbers remain simultaneously visible on the screen. Pressing [+] (full sequence: 4 [ENTER] 8 [×] 15 [ENTER] 3 [÷] [+]) combines them to yield 37. Zero writing, zero memory keys, zero working memory fatigue.

docs.title: 1.2 Zero Parentheses Syntax Errors
docs.text:
Elementary students have not mastered algebraic formal syntax. On standard in-fix calculators, entering: $\(2 + 3 \times 4\)$ yields either 20 (on cheap non-precedence calculators) or 14 (on algebraic hierarchy machines), creating profound confusion about what the machine is actually doing. In RPN, there is strictly no ambiguity and no parentheses keys: * If you mean add first: 2 [ENTER] 3 [+] 4 [×] = 20 * If you mean multiply first: 3 [ENTER] 4 [×] 2 [+] = 14

The student controls the order of operations explicitly, mirroring the natural mental decomposition taught in Singapore Math and Bridges.

docs.title: 1.3 Uniformity Across the K–12 Continuum
docs.text: By standardizing on a 4-stack XYZT display from Grade 1, students develop an intuitive spatial mental model of the stack that carries forward seamlessly to the flagship SC-32 Scientific Calculator in middle school, high school AP Physics, and collegiate engineering. There is zero unlearning.

docs.title: 1.4 Two-Stack Mode (\(Y, X\)) & Stack Depth Configuration Rubric
docs.text: While the 4-stack XYZT architecture is the default for general multi-step arithmetic, early elementary teachers can focus young learners on just the two active registers (Waiting Shelf Y and Workbench X): * Two-Row Place Value & Part-Whole Modeling (PLACE-01): On the Place Value Studio 6×2 tray, Row 1 (upper row) maps directly to Register \(Y\) and Row 0 (lower row) maps to Register \(X\). Focusing on \(Y\) and \(X\) creates an exact 1:1 spatial correspondence between the physical rows on the tray and the screen without the distraction of upper registers (\(Z, T\)). * Returning to Standard 4-Stack Number Mode: Pressing [NUM] (Whole Number Mode key at Row 3 Col 4) or [FDISP] immediately restores the default 4-stack XYZT operational display. * Manual Stack Depth Switching ([FLAGS] Key Rubric): Kindergarten and early Grade 1 teachers who want to keep cognitive load minimal across all arithmetic operations can manually switch the SC-6 into 2-stack mode at any time using the hardware configuration rubric: 1. Press [g] [FLAGS] to open the system configuration matrix. 2. Press digit [5] (5:DEP) to cycle stack depth between 4-LV (4-level XYZT) and 2-LV (2-level \(Y, X\)). 3. Press [C] (or [g] [FLAGS]) to dismiss the flags matrix and resume calculations with the chosen stack depth. (In the desktop and companion apps, clicking the LCD stack depth badge or opening the Flags menu provides the same direct toggle.)

docs.title: 2. Curricular Module 1: Integer Division with Remainders ([÷R])
docs.text: // STANDARDS ALIGNMENT CCSS-M: 4.OA.A.3, 4.NBT.B.6, 5.NBT.B.6 • TEKS: 4.4E, 4.4F, 5.3C • Singapore: Primary 3A Ch 3, Primary 4A Ch 2

docs.title: The Elementary Division Dilemma
docs.text:
In Grades 3 through 5, division is introduced as fair sharing with leftovers (quotient and remainder): $\(23 \div 4 = 5 \text{ R } 3\)$ When an elementary student enters \(23 \div 4\) on a standard smartphone or cheap school calculator, the screen displays: $\(5.75\)$ For a 9-year-old who has not yet learned decimal place value or fraction-to-decimal conversion, \(5.75\) is actively counter-productive. It fails to answer: * "How many full boxes of 4 can we pack?" (5 boxes) * "How many items are left over?" (3 items, not 0.75 items!)

Because of this, teachers routinely ban calculators during division units.

docs.title: The SC-6 Solution: The [÷R] Integer Division Key
docs.text:
The SC-6 provides a dedicated Integer Division with Remainder operator located at [g] [÷R] (legend ÷R):

        DIVIDEND                 DIVISOR                     OPERATION
   [2] [3] [ENTER]                 [4]                   [g] [÷R]  (÷R)
          |                         |                          |
          v                         v                          v
+-----------------+       +-----------------+        +-----------------+
| T:         0    |       | T:         0    |        | T:         0    |
| Z:         0    |       | Z:         0    |        | Z:         0    |
| Y:        23    |       | Y:        23    |        | Y:         3  <-- REMAINDER
| X:        23    |       | X:         4    |        | X:         5  <-- QUOTIENT
+-----------------+       +-----------------+        +-----------------+

docs.title: Keystroke Protocol & Display State
docs.text:
1. Enter Dividend: Type 23, press [ENTER].
  2. Enter Divisor: Type 4.
  3. Execute Integer Division: Press [g] [÷R] (full sequence: 23 [ENTER] 4 [g] [÷R]).
  4. Immediate Result:
  5. Register X displays the Quotient (5).
  6. Register Y displays the Remainder (3).
  7. Both values are visible at the same moment on the 4-line display!

docs.title: Swapping Quotient and Remainder ([x⇄y])
docs.text: If a follow-up calculation requires the remainder, the student does not need to retype it. Simply press [x⇄y] (the primary swap key): * X becomes 3 (Remainder ready for computation) * Y becomes 5 (Quotient preserved in stack)

docs.title: Classroom Investigation: Spool Slicing & Filament Leftovers
docs.text:
Scenario: A 5th-grade maker lab has a 1,000-gram spool of Sunlu Midnight Navy PLA filament. Each 3D-printed calculator housing requires exactly 82 grams. 1. How many complete calculator housings can the class 3D print? 2. How many grams of filament remain on the spool for calibration test chips?

  • Verified Keystroke Sequence: 1000 [ENTER] 82 [g] [÷R]
  • Verified Quotient (\(X\)): 12 complete calculator chassis printed!
  • Verified Remainder (\(Y\)): 16 grams of scrap / test filament remaining (T: 0 | Z: 0 | Y: 16 | X: 12).

docs.title: 3. Curricular Module 2: Instant Inverse Verification with [LASTX]
docs.text: // STANDARDS FOR MATHEMATICAL PRACTICE CCSS.MATH.PRACTICE.MP1: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them. CCSS.MATH.PRACTICE.MP3: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others. CCSS.MATH.PRACTICE.MP6: Attend to precision.

docs.title: The Misconception: "I Got an Answer, So I'm Done"
docs.text:
A persistent struggle in elementary math is teaching students to check their work using inverse operations: $\(\text{If } A + B = C \implies C - B = A\)$ $\(\text{If } A \times B = C \implies C \div B = A\)$

On standard calculators, as soon as the user presses =, the input operands vanish into the ether. Checking the answer requires re-entering the entire problem from scratch, which students find tedious and resist doing.

docs.title: The SC-6 Solution: The [LASTX] Key
docs.text:
The SC-6 maintains a hardware memory register called LASTX. Whenever an arithmetic operation (+, -, ×, ÷, ÷R, MOD) is executed, the calculator automatically copies the value that was in Register \(X\) right before the calculation into LASTX.

Pressing [f] [LASTX] pushes that saved operand back into Register \(X\), lifting the answer into Register \(Y\)!

docs.title: Recipe 1: Self-Checking Multi-Digit Addition
docs.text:
Student Task: Solve \(487 + 265\) and verify using inverse subtraction (487 [ENTER] 265 [+] [f] [LASTX] [-] → 487).

PHASE 1: SOLVE THE ADDITION
1. [4] [8] [7] [ENTER]    --> Y: 487 | X: 487
2. [2] [6] [5]            --> Y: 487 | X: 265
3. [+]                    --> X: 752  (Sum)
   [Calculator quietly stores 265 in LASTX]

PHASE 2: VERIFY WITH INVERSE SUBTRACTION (ONE KEYSTROKE!)
4. [f] [LASTX]            --> Y: 752 | X: 265  (Original addend retrieved!)
5. [-]                    --> X: 487  (Original starting number restored!)

Teacher Facilitation Prompt: "Did your screen return to 487? If yes, your addition is mathematically guaranteed to be correct. You proved it yourself without asking the teacher!"

docs.title: Recipe 2: The Complete Division Proof (\(Q \times D + R = \text{Dividend}\))
docs.text:
Student Task: Divide \(79 \div 8\) using [g] [÷R], then prove the result using [f] [LASTX] (79 [ENTER] 8 [g] [÷R] [f] [LASTX] [×] [+] → 79).

PHASE 1: INTEGER DIVISION
1. [7] [9] [ENTER] [8] [g] [÷R]
   SCREEN READOUT:
   Y: 7  (Remainder R)
   X: 9  (Quotient Q)
   [LASTX automatically holds the Divisor: 8]

PHASE 2: THE 3-KEYSTROKE PROOF
2. [f] [LASTX]            --> Z: 7 (R) | Y: 9 (Q) | X: 8 (Divisor D)
3. [×]                    --> Y: 7 (R) | X: 72 (Q × D)
4. [+]                    --> X: 79  (Original Dividend restored!)

This 3-keystroke verification sequence ([f] [LASTX] → [×] → [+]) concretizes the Division Algorithm identity: $\(\text{Dividend} = (\text{Quotient} \times \text{Divisor}) + \text{Remainder}\)$ Students actively experience how multiplication and addition undo division and subtraction.

docs.title: Recipe 3: Recovering from a Keystroke Slip
docs.text:
Elementary students frequently press the wrong operator by mistake (e.g., hitting [-] instead of [+]). On traditional calculators, they must press CLEAR and start over. On the SC-6 (150 [ENTER] 25 [-] [f] [LASTX] [+] [f] [LASTX] [+] → 175):

  • Problem: Student wants \(150 + 25\).
  • Mistake: They enter 150 [ENTER] 25 [-] and get 125.
  • Recovery:
  • Press [f] [LASTX] → 25 returns to \(X\), 125 lifts to \(Y\).
  • Press [+] → 150 (Starting base restored!).
  • Press [f] [LASTX] → 25 returns to \(X\), 150 lifts to \(Y\).
  • Press [+] → 175 (Correct sum reached without re-typing 150 or 25!).

docs.title: 4. Curricular Module 3: Rhythmic Skip-Counting with [REP]
docs.text: // STANDARDS ALIGNMENT CCSS-M: 2.OA.C.4, 3.OA.A.1, 3.OA.A.7 • Bridges: Grade 2 Unit 1, Grade 3 Unit 2 • Singapore: Primary 2A Ch 4, Primary 3A Ch 3

docs.title: Why Kinesthetic Rhythm Matters
docs.text:
Multiplication is fundamentally equal groups of items. Before children can memorize \(7 \times 6 = 42\), they must feel and hear the cadence of the sequence: $\(7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42\)$

The SC-6 features a dedicated Replication Key [REP] located at [g] [REP]. Pressing [g] [REP] populates every level of the 4-level stack with the active number: $\(T = K, \quad Z = K, \quad Y = K, \quad X = K\)$

Because an RPN 4-stack duplicates the \(T\) register when the stack drops during dyadic addition, pressing [+] repeatedly adds the constant indefinitely!

                     HOW [REP] CREATES AN INFINITE FACT LADDER

1. [7] [g] [REP]           2. PRESS [+]              3. PRESS [+] AGAIN
+---------------------+    +---------------------+    +---------------------+
| T:         7        |    | T:         7        |    | T:         7        |
| Z:         7        |    | Z:         7        |    | Z:         7        |
| Y:         7        |    | Y:         7        |    | Y:         7        |
| X:         7        |    | X:        14  (7×2) |    | X:        21  (7×3) |
+---------------------+    +---------------------+    +---------------------+
                                 (T duplicates on drop!)    (T duplicates on drop!)

docs.title: Classroom Activity: The Rhythm of Multiples
docs.text:
1. Teacher Prompt: "Let's build the 6-times multiplication ladder up to 60."
  2. Setup: Student types 6 [g] [REP]. All 4 stack registers are now primed with 6.
  3. Execution: The student chants aloud with each tactile snap:
  4. Press [+] → "6 times 2 is 12!" (Screen: 12)
  5. Press [+] → "6 times 3 is 18!" (Screen: 18)
  6. Press [+] → "6 times 4 is 24!" (Screen: 24)
  7. Press [+] → "6 times 5 is 30!" (Screen: 30)
  8. Press [+] → "6 times 6 is 36!" (Screen: 36)
  9. Press [+] → "6 times 7 is 42!" (Screen: 42)
  10. Press [+] → "6 times 8 is 48!" (Screen: 48)
  11. Press [+] → "6 times 9 is 54!" (Screen: 54)
  12. Press [+] → "6 times 10 is 60!" (Screen: 60)

The 400-gram snap-dome keys deliver an audible acoustic "click" and physical tactile feedback that anchors the auditory chant to muscle memory.

docs.title: Exploration A: Backwards Countdown Ladders (Subtracting Constantly)
docs.text: Task: Start at 100, skip-count backwards by 8. 1. Enter starting point: 100 [ENTER]. 2. Prime the subtrahend: 8 [g] [REP]. 3. Press [-] repeatedly: * Press [-] → 92 * Press [-] → 84 * Press [-] → 76 * Press [-] → 68 ... down to 4 (the remainder of \(100 \div 8\)!).

docs.title: Exploration B: Geometric Exponential Doubling (Powers of 2)
docs.text: Task: Discover exponential growth (doubling lily pads on a pond). 1. Prime the base: 2 [g] [REP]. 2. Press [×] repeatedly: * Press [×] → 4 (\(2^2\)) * Press [×] → 8 (\(2^3\)) * Press [×] → 16 (\(2^4\)) * Press [×] → 32 (\(2^5\)) * Press [×] → 64 (\(2^6\)) * Press [×] → 128 (\(2^7\)) ... up to 1024 (\(2^{10}\))!

docs.title: 5. Curricular Module 4: Order of Operations without Parentheses
docs.text: // STANDARDS ALIGNMENT CCSS-M: 5.OA.A.1, 6.EE.A.2 • Big Ideas Math: Grade 5 Ch 1, Grade 6 Ch 3

docs.title: Multi-Term Word Problem Example
docs.text:
Scenario: A school STEM club buys: * 3 microcontrollers at $4.50 each * 2 battery holders at $1.25 each * 4 LED packs at $0.75 each

What is the total cost of the order? $\(\text{Total} = (3 \times 4.50) + (2 \times 1.25) + (4 \times 0.75)\)$

docs.title: How Infix vs. SC-6 4-Stack Handles the Problem (3 [ENTER] 4.5 [×] 2 [ENTER] 1.25 [×] [+] 4 [ENTER] 0.75 [×] [+] → 19)
docs.text:
Step Traditional Infix Calculator SC-6 4-Stack XYZT (RPN) Stack Registers (\(T, Z, Y, X\)) 1 Press ( 3 × 4.50 ) + (Must remember parentheses!) 3 [ENTER] 4.5 [×] \(X: 13.50\) 2 Press ( 2 × 1.25 ) + (Hope parentheses don't nest wrong!) 2 [ENTER] 1.25 [×] \(Y: 13.50, \quad X: 2.50\) 3 Press ( 4 × 0.75 ) = [+] \(X: 16.00\) (Running total!) 4 Hope order-of-operations evaluated correctly 4 [ENTER] 0.75 [×] \(Y: 16.00, \quad X: 3.00\) 5 — [+] \(X: 19\) (Final total verified!)

The Pedagogical Difference: On the SC-6, students never type a parenthesis. Every sub-calculation is evaluated immediately, and the intermediate products wait patiently on the screen. The child can pause at Step 2 and see both $13.50 and $2.50 resting on the screen.

docs.title: 5.5 Curricular Module 5: SC-6 Tutorial Mode (?) & Two-Method Verification
docs.text:
// TWO-METHOD VERIFICATION & WORKBOOK INTEGRATION Published Block Studios: PLACE-01, FRAC-01, PRIME-01 • Tutorial Keycap: [↰] [C] (Question Mark in a Circle ?)

Many upper-elementary and middle-school learners resist solving the same problem in multiple ways because traditional worksheets punish extra strategies with twice the handwriting. The 114-Page Big Ideas Math Daily Supplement (.PDF) turns multi-method verification into a structured two-step habit:

  • 1st Way (+10 pts): Solve Question \(N\) using your primary method (Big Ideas textbook method, physical block kit—PLACE-01, FRAC-01, or PRIME-01—or SC-6 RPN) and record +10 pts in the worksheet scoring box.
  • 2nd Way (+20 pts Double Points): Verify the exact same question using a second method (checking your block/paper work on the SC-6 stack or in SC-6 Tutorial Mode [↰] [C]) to earn +20 pts.

docs.text:

docs.title: Challenge Card 1: The Cookie Bakery Box Packing (Grades 3–4)
docs.text: Prompt: A baker bakes 58 chocolate chip cookies. Each gift box holds 6 cookies. 1. Use [g] [÷R] on your SC-6 to find how many full gift boxes she can pack. 2. How many cookies are left over for the baker to eat? 3. Press [f] [LASTX] [×] [+] to prove your answer matches 58! Expected Keystrokes: 58 [ENTER] 6 [g] [÷R] ==> X: 9 boxes, Y: 4 leftover cookies. Proof: 58 [ENTER] 6 [g] [÷R] [f] [LASTX] [×] [+] ==> 58 cookies.

docs.title: Challenge Card 2: The Multiplication Table 7s Race (Grades 2–3)
docs.text: Prompt: Load 7 into your SC-6 using [g] [REP]. 1. Press [+] four times. What multiple of 7 is on the screen? (\(7 \times 5 = 35\)) 2. Press [+] three more times. What is \(7 \times 8\)? (\(56\)) 3. Can you reach 70 without making an error? Expected Keystrokes: 7 [g] [REP] [+] [+] [+] [+] ==> 35. [+] [+] [+] ==> 56.

docs.title: Challenge Card 3: The Detective Proof Station (Grades 4–5)
docs.text: Prompt: A student calculated \(345 + 189 = 534\). 1. Enter 345 [ENTER] 189 [+] on your SC-6. 2. Use [f] [LASTX] to recall the second addend. 3. Press [-] to perform the inverse operation (345 [ENTER] 189 [+] [f] [LASTX] [-]). Did you get 345? 4. Write an explanation: Why does LASTX guarantee the answer is correct?

docs.title: Summary: Empowering Young Mathematicians
docs.text: The transition to a default 4-stack XYZT display in the SC-6 transforms the calculator from a passive answer generator into an active, transparent laboratory instrument. With [÷R], [LASTX], and [REP], young students explore the fundamental structures of arithmetic—quotients, remainders, inverses, and multiples—with tactile certainty and joy.

docs.text:
